newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian ship missing off Libyan coast.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian ship missing off Libyan coast.

text.p: An Egyptian merchant ship with a crew of 12 has gone missing in the Mediterranean on a voyage from Alexandria to the port of Trapani in western Sicily, Egyptian foreign ministry officials said on Sunday.
Egypt has asked the Libyan authorities to launch a thorough search of the Libyan coast after failed attempts to locate the ship, the Samir, in the open sea, they added.
An Egyptian government newspaper said the owners last made contact with the ship on March 12, five days after it sailed from Alexandria. No distress signal has been received.
The owners at first thought the vessel may have put into a small port because of bad weather but inquiries to their agents in Greece, Italy, Malta, Libya and Tunisia drew a blank.
Shipping company director Sameh el-Badramani told the newspaper Akhbar el-Yom that he did not rule piracy but pirates usually stole just the cargo and not the ship itself.
The Samir was carrying a cargo of Egyptian salt. The tonnage of the vessel and the name of the company which owns it were not immediately available.
